results.summary:
The attempt row in the run comment now carries the agent session behind it. Draft PR #28 (branch worktree-kb-18-2, "Closes #18").

`hkb hook stop` writes session_id + transcript_path onto the attempt row on its first call, before the status check so a finished attempt (the one a human actually reopens) is covered too; a marker at .kanban/sessions/<n>-<k> keeps it to a single read + PATCH, so the 2nd and 3rd Stop-hook firings cost nothing. Nudge logic untouched. In loop mode, watchChild parses the tail of the worker log (`claude -p --output-format json` signs off with one JSON object) and folds session_id/total_cost_usd/num_turns/duration_ms into the save it was already making; the parse is in its own try/catch so a malformed log can never cost the protocol_violation reclaim. `hkb show <n>` prints `session <id> · $0.42 · 37 turns · 6m12s` and a `cd .claude/worktrees/kb-<n>-<k> && claude --resume <id>` line per attempt.

New pure functions in src/model.js: parseSessionLog, sessionUpdate (the record-once decision), formatSession, resumeCommand, worktreePath, plus the SESSION_FIELDS list.

For the next worker: cost/turns only appear for profiles the dispatcher watches (claude-p in loop mode). The default `claude-bg` profile is fire-and-forget with no result JSON in its log, so those attempts get session_id from the Stop hook only. If cost on bg attempts is wanted, src/jobs.js already surfaces `sessionId` (and `tokens`) from the job listing/state.json — the reclaim loop in dispatch.js could fold that in for free at a point where it already saves, but I left that delicate loop alone deliberately (it is the code behind the #15/3 and #14/2 regressions).
